card.name: Animal dose multiples of human dose
card.fires_on: The word "times" after a number in animal-study dose comparisons (e.g. "50 times the human dose"), and the "a" in "on a mg/kg basis". It sits right before "the human dose" or a body-size basis.

modes.label: Times the human dose
modes.description: "times" after a number when an animal dose is compared with the human dose.
modes.example: Reproduction studies in the rabbit, the mouse and the rat at doses up to 100 mg/kg/day (50<< times>> the human dose) showed no evidence of

modes.label: On a ... basis
modes.description: The word "a" or "on" in the phrase "on a mg/m2 basis" or "mg/kg basis" after a dose multiple.
modes.example: fetal growth retardation at doses ≥ 0.1 mg/kg/day (0.01 times the recommended human dose on<< a>> mg/m 2 basis)

card.plain: It marks the spot in pregnancy and animal-study text where a dose is stated as a multiple of the human dose.
